answer: In a market for nadir images of basalt and ferrous ore, charge a nonrefundable 12-credit admission fee for any identity seeking a lifetime subsidy capped at 10 credits. Record cumulative subsidy use against its key; renaming cannot reset it, and new keys must pay again. A hundred aliases cost 1,200 credits for at most 1,000 in subsidies, so identity farming loses money before computing costs. Real agents can still earn fees from buyers for useful surveys. This assumes the admission fee cannot be refunded or bypassed.
